transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. Welcome in—what brings you here today?

I came in because I can’t seem to stay focused on one thing at work anymore. I’ll be doing an estimate or filling out a code form, then a tool makes noise, I get a text, or I have some new idea about the workshop, and I’m off on that instead. Then I start mixing up different jobs.
Thinking back, did you have similar trouble staying focused and getting distracted when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's only been happening recently?

No, this feels more recent. Lately I’ll be working on an estimate or a code form, and a tool noise or a text—or some idea about the workshop—pulls me away. Then I come back and I’ve mixed up which job I was working on.
Over these recent weeks, have you also been feeling unusually sad, down, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling especially down or anything like that.
Have you noticed times recently where you felt unusually energetic, upbeat, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with your mind racing with ideas?

Yeah. For the last few months I’ve only been sleeping maybe three or four hours, then I’m up before dawn feeling ready to go—pricing materials, answering emails, sketching out another system. It doesn’t feel like I missed sleep; I feel like I had a full night.

During this period of high energy and reduced sleep, has it caused serious problems at work or in your relationships—like conflicts, risky decisions, or trouble completing your responsibilities—or has anyone said you seemed 'too much' or out of control?

Yeah, it’s causing problems. Clients have complained about missed details and schedules getting mixed up, and my apprentices don’t really trust my direction like they used to. At home, my wife and I are arguing constantly about the mortgage and the business. She thinks I’m putting everything we built at risk.

Aside from these last few months, have you ever had an earlier period—months or years ago—where you went through a similar stretch of high energy or, alternatively, a spell of prolonged low mood or depression?
No, I can’t think of an earlier time like this. It’s really been building over about seven months, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment.

During this stretch of high energy, have you experienced anything like hearing or seeing things others didn't notice, or holding beliefs—like having special powers or a special mission—that others found unrealistic or hard to believe?

I haven’t heard or seen things. But I do keep feeling like I can take on commercial jobs and train a whole crew right now. Part of me knows my licensing and experience aren’t really where they need to be for all of that, but I still feel like I can handle it.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a first lifetime episode (no prior manic, hypomanic, or depressive episodes) lasting approximately 7 months, characterized by decreased need for sleep (3-4 hours without fatigue), increased energy and goal-directed activity, distractibility, grandiosity (belief he can take on commercial jobs and train a crew beyond his actual licensing/experience), and significant functional impairment in work (client complaints, apprentice distrust) and marital relationship (constant conflict). No psychotic symptoms (hallucinations or bizarre delusions) were present, and no depressive symptoms were endorsed. Since there is no history of prior mood episodes, this is classified as a single manic episode without psychotic symptoms (F30.1) rather than bipolar disorder (which requires recurrent episodes). ADHD was considered given distractibility but ruled out due to lack of childhood onset and presence of concurrent mood/energy/sleep changes pointing to a manic syndrome.
